import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 769

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/769](https://www.erdosproblems.com/769)
-/

namespace Erdos769

open Filter

open scoped Topology

/-- An axis-parallel homothetic copy of the standard `n`-cube. -/
structure Cube (n : ℕ) where
  lower : Fin n → ℝ
  side : ℝ

/-- Membership in the half-open cube `∏ j, [lower j, lower j + side)`. -/
def Cube.Mem {n : ℕ} (Q : Cube n) (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, Q.lower j ≤ x j ∧ x j < Q.lower j + Q.side

/-- Membership in the half-open unit cube `[0,1)^n`. -/
def InUnit {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ j, 0 ≤ x j ∧ x j < 1

/-- A cube is nondegenerate and contained in the closed unit cube. -/
def Cube.InsideUnit {n : ℕ} (Q : Cube n) : Prop :=
  0 < Q.side ∧ ∀ j, 0 ≤ Q.lower j ∧ Q.lower j + Q.side ≤ 1

/-- `tiles` is an exact decomposition of the unit `n`-cube into `k` homothetic
cubes: every tile is a positive homothet inside the unit cube, and every point
of `[0,1)^n` belongs to exactly one half-open tile. -/
def IsTiling {n k : ℕ} (tiles : Fin k → Cube n) : Prop :=
  (∀ i, (tiles i).InsideUnit) ∧ ∀ x, InUnit x → ∃! i, (tiles i).Mem x

/-- Exactly `k` homothetic `n`-cubes can tile the unit `n`-cube. -/
def Admissible (n k : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ tiles : Fin k → Cube n, IsTiling tiles

/-- `c` is the minimal cutoff `c(n)`: every `k ≥ c` is admissible, and (when
`c > 0`) `c - 1` is not. -/
def IsCutoff (n c : ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ k, c ≤ k → Admissible n k) ∧ (c = 0 ∨ ¬Admissible n (c - 1))

/-- The highlighted conjecture `c(n) ≫ n^n`: there is an absolute positive
constant `A/B` with `c(n) ≥ (A/B) n^n` for all sufficiently large `n`. -/
def Erdos769LowerBound : Prop :=
  ∃ A B N : ℕ, 0 < A ∧ 0 < B ∧
    ∀ n c : ℕ, N ≤ n → IsCutoff n c → A * n ^ n ≤ B * c

/--
Let $c(n)$ be minimal such that if $k\geq c(n)$ then the $n$-dimensional unit
cube can be decomposed into $k$ homothetic $n$-dimensional cubes. Give good
bounds for $c(n)$ — in particular, is it true that $c(n)\gg n^n$?

The `c(n) \gg n^n` conjecture is **false**: for odd `n`, one can tile the unit
`n`-cube into `k` homothetic cubes for every `k ≥ U(n)` with `U(n)/n^n → 0`, so
`c(n)/n^n → 0` along odd dimensions and no absolute constant lower-bounds it.

Determining good bounds for `c(n)` in general remains open.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/williamjblair/lean-proofs/blob/4f915a323443bfb1709a6805a013812016dca88a/starfleet/erdos-769/Research/Solution.lean"]
theorem erdos_769 : answer(False) ↔ Erdos769LowerBound := by
  sorry

/--
What refuting $c(n)\gg n^n$ leaves open: give good bounds for $c(n)$. Asked here on the
scale the problem itself sets, $n^n$: does $c$ have a well-defined order
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{\log c(n)}{n\log n}?$$
The refuted conjecture would have forced this limit to be at least $1$.
The cutoff condition is restricted to positive dimensions: in dimension zero,
exact coverage permits only one tile, so no cutoff exists.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_769.variants.growth_rate :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∃ c : ℕ → ℕ, (∀ n, 0 < n → IsCutoff n (c n)) ∧
        ∃ γ : ℝ, Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => Real.log (c n) / (n * Real.log n)) atTop (𝓝 γ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos769

findings.description: The remaining request for good bounds has been specialized to a new regularity question: whether log(c(n))/(n log n) converges to some finite real γ. The answer slot is a proposition deciding existence of a limit; it does not ask to determine γ or specify bounds. This is not an equivalent formulation of obtaining good bounds: sharp bounds can accommodate oscillation and need not imply convergence at this scale. It could be a useful independent variant, but I could not substantiate its attribution to the cited problem.
findings.source_evidence: The independent transcription at https://huggingface.co/datasets/stalaei/Erdosh-problems, row Er74b-14 (August 2025), asks: “Give good bounds for c(n); in particular, is c(n) ≫ n^n?” Erdős, Remarks on some problems in number theory, §II, pp. 199–200, https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf, discusses improved bounds and specifically predicts c(n)>n^n when n+1 is prime. Neither text introduces the normalized logarithmic limit. The live erdosproblems.com page and forum returned Cloudflare challenges, so their current additional remarks could not be checked.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide a source actually posing this limit-existence question and distinguish it from the original request for bounds, or omit this variant. A source-backed remaining variant could instead address Erdős's prime-successor lower-bound conjecture, with its intended dimensional range.

reformulations.difference: The source's geometric decomposition is represented by unique membership in half-open, axis-parallel cubes rather than coverage by closed cubes with pairwise disjoint interiors.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite family of positive-side-length cubes, closed coverage with disjoint interiors gives unique half-open coverage: perturb a point of [0,1)^n a sufficiently small distance in every positive coordinate direction, smaller than all relevant positive gaps to tile faces. The covering tile then contains the original point half-open. Two half-open tiles containing that point would have overlapping interiors after such a perturbation. Conversely, taking closures of the finite half-open union gives closed coverage, and interior overlap would contradict unique half-open membership. InsideUnit supplies positivity and containment; unique coverage also prevents duplicate tiles.

reformulations.difference: Minimality is expressed by eventual admissibility together with inadmissibility of c−1, instead of using a minimum operation or a cutoff function.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved IsCutoff n c ↔ IsLeast {d : ℕ | ∀ k, d ≤ k → Admissible n k} c. If a smaller threshold d existed, c−1 would be admissible. Conversely, admissibility of c−1 together with admissibility of every k≥c would make c−1 a smaller threshold. The explicit c=0 case handles truncated subtraction correctly.

reformulations.difference: The Vinogradov lower bound is encoded using positive natural numbers A,B, cross-multiplied inequalities, and quantification over cutoff witnesses rather than a fixed real constant and a named c(n).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved the equivalence with a positive real constant lower-bounding a fixed cutoff function eventually. Every positive real constant admits a smaller positive rational 1/(D+1), while positive A/B yields the corresponding real inequality by cross-multiplication. Cutoffs are unique, and I separately proved that a cutoff exists in every positive dimension using regular-grid substitutions and a numerical-semigroup conductor. Dimension zero has no cutoff, but may be excluded by increasing the eventual threshold N.

review.notes: No confirmed mathematical defect was found in the cube definitions, cutoff definition, or main negative lower-bound statement. Lean checks established Admissible n 1, failure of Admissible n 0, Admissible 0 k ↔ k=1, absence of zero-dimensional cutoffs, cutoff uniqueness and positivity, and a two-interval tiling. The logarithm/division defaults at n=0,1 affect only finitely many terms. I rebuilt the cited disproof, both with its original definitions and against the committed FC definitions; its axioms are only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Thus the formal_proof record and negative answer are substantiated for the broader all-dimensions question. This does not disprove the distinct prime-successor conjecture in Erdős's original paper. The live cited page remained inaccessible despite descriptive User-Agent headers; today's website status and full remarks could not be independently read. All experiments were placed under /workspace/review, and the reviewed file was not modified.
